content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define key genetic terms: allele, dominant, recessive, genotype, phenotype
Explain the difference between homozygous and heterozygous
Use correct genetic terminology to describe inheritance

Genetics has its own vocabulary that is essential for understanding inheritance. These terms are used to describe genes, their variants, and how they affect characteristics. Mastering this terminology is crucial for understanding genetic crosses and inheritance patterns.
is a section of DNA that codes for a particular characteristic (by coding for a specific protein).
There is a gene that determines whether you can roll your tongue.
is a version (variant) of a gene.
Different alleles of a gene produce different versions of a characteristic
You inherit one allele from each parent
Alleles are found at the same position (locus) on homologous chromosomes
The tongue rolling gene has two alleles:
One allele for tongue rolling (can roll)

attrs.alt: Homologous chromosomes showing alleles at the same locus

content.text: allele is always expressed in the phenotype, even when only one copy is present.
Only one copy needed to show the characteristic
"Masks" the effect of the recessive allele
allele is only expressed when two copies are present (no dominant allele).
Two copies needed to show the characteristic
Is "masked" by the dominant allele when heterozygous
is the genetic makeup of an organism - the combination of alleles it has.
Written using letters (e.g., TT, Tt, tt)
is the physical expression of the genotype - the observable characteristics.
What you can see or measure
Described in words (e.g., "can roll tongue", "blue eyes")
means having two identical alleles for a gene.
because they always pass on the same allele.
means having two different alleles for a gene.
Heterozygous individuals can pass on either allele to their offspring.
is a person who has one copy of a recessive allele but does not show the characteristic.
They can pass the recessive allele to offspring
A person with genotype Cc for cystic fibrosis:
Has one normal allele (C) and one CF allele (c)
Does not have cystic fibrosis (C is dominant)
Is a carrier and can pass on the c allele
Section of DNA coding for a characteristic
Blue eye allele, brown eye allele
Allele expressed with one or two copies
Allele expressed only with two copies
Use the same letter for both alleles of a gene
Recessive = lowercase of the same letter
Choose a letter that makes sense (often first letter of dominant trait)
Avoid letters where capital and lowercase look similar (like S/s or C/c can be confusing)
R for rolling, N for non-rolling (different letters - wrong!)
A plant has the genotype Rr for seed shape, where R is round (dominant) and r is wrinkled (recessive).
Is the plant homozygous or heterozygous?
What alleles can this plant pass to offspring?
Two parents both have brown eyes (genotype Bb). What phenotypes are possible in their children?
Possible phenotypes: Brown eyes OR blue eyes
Sometimes neither allele is dominant over the other - both are expressed. This is called
IA and IB are co-dominant to each other
IAIB produces blood group AB (both expressed)
Dominant alleles are more common than recessive alleles
Dominant refers to how alleles interact, not their frequency. Recessive alleles can be very common in a population.
Dominant simply means the allele is expressed in heterozygotes. Recessive alleles can code for perfectly normal traits.
Genotype and phenotype are the same thing
Genotype is the alleles (Tt); phenotype is the characteristic shown (tongue roller)
Heterozygous means the organism is "half and half"
In heterozygotes with complete dominance, only the dominant phenotype is shown
Section of DNA coding for a characteristic
Allele expressed when one or two copies present
Allele only expressed when two copies present
Heterozygote for a recessive allele who doesn't show the trait
Position of a gene on a chromosome
When both alleles are expressed in heterozygotes
An allele is a version of a gene
Dominant alleles are expressed with one or two copies (written as capitals)
Recessive alleles are only expressed with two copies (written as lowercase)
Genotype = alleles present; Phenotype = observable characteristic
Homozygous = two identical alleles; Heterozygous = two different alleles
Carriers are heterozygous for recessive conditions but appear unaffected
